SystemSketch · implementation report · 2026-09-01

You can change how things look now

SystemSketch ships with tldraw's style panel switched off, so until now a shape's colour, fill, stroke, size, typeface, alignment, routing and endpoints could not be changed on canvas at all. The selection pill now carries them, laid out the way FigJam lays them out, over tldraw's own styles — and, since the second pass in §7, at FigJam's own sizes, with FigJam's own picker behind a Custom cell.

18/18 browser checks 32 appearance unit tests 14 FigJam readings equal their tokens 11 controls · 0 new shape props tldraw 5.3.2, unforked
The closed vocabulary is still the feature. Every option is a value tldraw's style system already accepts, so the menu can only ever ask for a state a shape can actually hold. The picker does not break that: a colour it produces becomes a named colour on tldraw's enum, registered through the same theme API the palette uses, and the name carries the hex so the file describes its own colours.

1 · What it does

2 · The controls

11 controls over stock tldraw styles. No new shape props, no schema change, nothing that would move the boundary this repo guards.

// The write path, straight out of tldraw's own style panel
editor.markHistoryStoppingPoint('appearance')
editor.run(() => {
  if (editor.isIn('select')) editor.setStyleForSelectedShapes(style, value)
  editor.setStyleForNextShapes(style, value)
})

3 · Copying FigJam's own values

A first pass copied FigJam's layout and drew everything else by hand. Zach looked at it and named four things that were still wrong. Each was fixed by reading the value out of FigJam rather than by judging it — and one of them was a claim of mine that turned out to be false.

The palette: I said this needed a fork. It does not.

FigJam: 21 colours in an 11×2 grid, plus a Custom picker.

I had said FigJam's palette would need a custom colour StyleProp, that a custom style prop means replacing tldraw's built-in shape utils, and that replacing shape utils is a fork — so the answer was tldraw's thirteen. That reasoning was wrong at the first step. tldraw derives the colour style from the theme: <Tldraw themes={...}> calls registerColorsFromThemes before any effect runs or any store loads, and that function calls DefaultColorStyle.addValues(...) for every colour a theme names. The palette is a documented prop on the stock component. No shape util is replaced, no schema forked.

The subtlety is in the same function's other half: it also removes any registered colour absent from every theme. A palette of only FigJam's names would unregister tldraw's grey, and a board that had ever stored a grey shape would fail validation on load. So the theme spreads DEFAULT_THEME rather than replacing it — all thirteen stay registered, and the menu simply shows FigJam's 21. (§7 found the same removal biting from a second direction.)

The hexes are sampled from FigJam's own popover: the centre pixel of each 24px swatch, located from the panel geometry rather than by eye.

The icons: traced, not approximated

FigJam: filled paths on a 24×24 viewBox, drawn with a CSS variable.

53 icons are captured from the running application. FigJam's option cells are unlabelled divs, so an icon's meaning only exists in its tooltip: the tracer hovers each cell, reads the tooltip, and reads the SVG under the cursor, so every path arrives already paired with FigJam's own word for it rather than by counting positions in a screenshot.

Keys are namespaced by control, and that is not tidiness. FigJam calls two different icons Triangle — a shape in the library, an outline arrowhead in the endpoint list — and a first cut keyed on the bare name, which silently drew arrowheads in the shape picker. The failure was silent because an unknown key falls back to a drawn glyph rather than throwing, so src/appearance/figjamIconMap.test.ts now fails on any name that was not traced.

Arrowheads mirror on the end control: FigJam draws one set of six and flips it for the far end, so the icon always points the way the arrow travels.

The control order follows the arrow

FigJam: Change color | Line style | Add text | Start point | Line shape | End point.

Where the arrow leaves, how it travels, where it lands. The first pass put the line shape ahead of both ends. This was already in the capture — the frames are named 04-start-point, 05-line-shape, 06-end-point — and had simply not been read.

Three line shapes, because we have three

FigJam: Elbowed · Curved · Straight.

The menu showed two. SystemSketch's own cable style has carried exactly FigJam's three all along — CONNECTION_ROUTING_KINDS is curved / straight / elbow — and the appearance menu had simply never surfaced it. It does now, so a cable reaches the full vocabulary, while a stock tldraw arrow keeps the two kinds it actually has. Offering a third to a shape that cannot hold one would be the failure mode this whole model exists to avoid.

4 · Where it deliberately differs from FigJam

6 decisions worth arguing with. Each is a consequence of building on tldraw's styles rather than a shortcut, and each is reversible.

One colour, not two

FigJam: FigJam gives a shape a separate stroke colour and fill colour, each with its own palette; its shape Line style popover repeats the palette under Solid / Dashed / None.

tldraw has a single color per shape that tints both. Repeating the grid under Line style would be two controls writing one value — an alias that reads as a bug the first time you change one and the other moves. Colour lives in the colour popover only; a shape's Line style is the chip row alone.

Every value, not FigJam's subset

FigJam: FigJam's stroke styles are Solid / Dashed / None; its connector weights are Thin / Thick; its font sizes end in Huge.

A menu that cannot show a state the document can hold is broken, not tidy. tldraw's default dash is draw: hide it and a freshly drawn shape opens its own popover with nothing selected. tldraw's middle two weights and its four-rung size ladder are shown the same way, and Huge has no rung to sit on.

Size is one control, not two

FigJam: FigJam has a stroke weight (2 values, connectors only) and a font size (5 values) as separate controls.

In tldraw size drives both. On a shape it is presented as FigJam's Font size; on a connector it is the weight inside Line style. That is a presentational grouping of one prop, not a split of it: setting a connector's weight also sets its label's size, and splitting them would need a custom style prop and a schema change, which is the boundary this repo deliberately keeps.

Opacity is a shape property, not a colour channel

FigJam: FigJam's picker has an alpha slider on the colour itself.

The slider is there and drives tldraw's own setOpacityForSelectedShapes, which fades the whole shape, label included. It is the stock API, one undo step per drag, and the one place the two colour models differ.

A Block contributes nothing, but does not block its neighbours

FigJam: n/a — FigJam has no equivalent of a Block.

A Block defines its own style props (systemsketch:blockView and friends) and none of tldraw's, so it has no appearance to edit and the Block-only pill is unchanged. Selected alongside a rectangle, the pill now counts the whole selection and marks the S / P / E group as the Blocks' — see §7. What a Block's colour should mean is a decision, not a default; it is left open below.

Typography shows before there is text

FigJam: FigJam only grows the typography group once a shape actually has a label, and on a connector with a label it moves Line style after the text controls.

tldraw reports font and alignment as relevant for any geo shape or arrow, since every one can carry a label. Following tldraw here means you can set the type before you type, and a connector keeps its no-label order; it is a deviation, not an oversight.

5 · Live proof

npm run test:appearance drives the real product composition on an isolated board. Every change is checked against two oracles: the pill's own label, which comes from useRelevantStyles() and so round-trips through the document, and the painted stroke attribute on the canvas. A change that only moved the UI fails. The second pass added FigJam's geometry as a third: trigger widths, cell sizes, the two purples, the picker's bands.

  • PASSa selected shape gets shape, paint and typography controls, in FigJam order and at FigJam's widths
  • PASSthe colour popover stacks the fill row over the palette at FigJam's pitch, 8px above the pill, with a Custom cell
  • PASSchoosing a colour repaints the shape and rings the chosen swatch
  • PASSthe fill row and the palette write different styles from one popover
  • PASSCustom opens FigJam's 184x310 picker flush under the palette, on the current colour
  • PASStyping a hex applies it as a custom colour: the shape, the trigger and the Custom cell all show it
  • PASSdragging the saturation/value square repaints the shape live, as one history step
  • PASSthe opacity slider writes tldraw's shape opacity, and undoes as one step
  • PASSa board naming a custom colour saves the hex in the file and reopens painted with it
  • PASSa shape's Line style is a row of labelled chips offering every dash the document can hold
  • PASSFont size lists each rung at its own size and names the chosen one on its trigger; Typeface keeps Aa
  • PASSthe shape picker changes a rectangle into an ellipse
  • PASSeach appearance change is one history step
  • PASSa connector's Line style holds weight beside dash in one 44px popover, and both write through
  • PASSa connector gets routing and endpoints, and an endpoint applies
  • PASSa selection that disagrees reports mixed instead of one shape's value
  • PASSa Block selected beside a shape keeps the shape's appearance reachable, and the pill counts the whole selection
  • PASSthe physical journey produced zero local console errors
One bug this found is worth keeping in mind. TldrawUiPopover computes its open state as open || isOpen — it ORs any open prop with its own useMenuIsOpen. A component that also tracks the state can therefore open a popover but never close it, and clicking the trigger again does nothing. The fix is to pass neither prop and style on Radix's data-state="open".

7 · The second pass: the chrome, read from the DOM

The handoff left five tasks. Four are done here and the fifth is a question. The method did not change: every value below was read out of FigJam's running editor over the DevTools Protocol (tools/figjam/chrome_trace.py, which dumps the pill and each popover as a DOM tree with computed styles and path data), and the build of this page checks each reading against the token the product carries. It refuses to publish if any pair disagrees.

Two of these corrected the first pass rather than extending it. Cells in an icon row are 24px on a 32px pitch, not 32px on 36; and there are two purples — #9747ff for a labelled chip, #8a38f5 for an icon cell and for the ring around the chosen swatch — where the first pass had used one. A trigger is 56px because the 24px icon is butted straight against the 16px chevron with 8px either side, and the colour trigger is 54px because its 18px swatch sits in a 22px ring box instead. The Fill chips and the Solid / Dashed / None chips are two different components in FigJam (a 24px icon with no left padding; a 16px icon in a 24px slot with 4px before it) and are kept as two here.

Task 1 · Custom colour

“I think we can just save the hex into like the metadata or something in the file so that it can be loaded?” Zach, mid-task, on the open question of how a custom colour should persist.

That is what is built, with one refinement: the hex is saved in the colour's name, on every shape that uses it, rather than in a registry beside them. tldraw's color is a closed enum, so a picked colour has to become a named colour before any shape can hold it; naming it custom-a3f2c1 means the file describes its own colours, nothing can drift between a registry and the shapes, and the answer to “which build can open this board” is simply “any build that knows the prefix”. The unbounded, faithful option was taken over a fixed set of slots, because slot reuse would have silently recoloured other shapes; the cost is that a session registers one theme entry per distinct hex it ever previews, which is a kilobyte apiece. 

export function registerCustomColors(names: Iterable<string>, editor?: Editor): string[] {
  const added: string[] = []
  for (const name of names) {
    const hex = customColorHex(name)
    if (!hex) continue
    if (addThemeColor(name, hex)) added.push(name)
  }
  const registered = DefaultColorStyle.values as readonly string[]
  const unregistered = added.filter((name) => !registered.includes(name))
  if (unregistered.length > 0) {
    // Registers every colour the theme names and removes none, because the
    // theme is a spread of tldraw's own plus everything ever added here.
    registerColorsFromThemes(SYSTEMSKETCH_THEMES)
  }
  if (added.length > 0 && editor) {
    // A fresh object, so the theme atom changes identity and every swatch and
    // shape reading `getCurrentTheme()` re-renders with the new colour.
    editor.updateThemes({
      default: {
        ...FIGJAM_THEME,
        colors: { light: { ...FIGJAM_THEME.colors.light }, dark: { ...FIGJAM_THEME.colors.dark } },
      },
    })
  }
  return added
}

The store validates before it loads, so a saved board naming custom-a3f2c1 would fail to parse unless the name were registered first. Every load path — src/workspace/LocalWorkspace.tsx, src/embed/EmbeddedCanvas.tsx, src/previewClone.ts — therefore scans the raw text for custom names and registers them before parsing. The journey proves the round trip: type a hex, wait for the autosave, confirm the file contains "custom-a3f2c1", reopen the board, and read the colour back off the pill and the painted stroke.

Found on the way: a board in FigJam's teal could not be reopened

Baseline: a board painted in any of FigJam's nine names tldraw does not ship (teal, pink, dark-gray, gray, light-gray, light-orange, light-yellow, light-teal, light-pink) failed to load with invalidRecords.

parseTldrawJsonFile, which every load path uses, creates a throwaway store of its own with no themes. That store's registerColorsFromThemes resolves to tldraw's DEFAULT_THEME alone and — the removal half of §3 again — unregisters every other name, custom or FigJam's, on the very parse that would load them. The first pass never reloaded a board, so nothing caught it. The one object every registration path resolves through is DEFAULT_THEME, so the palette and every custom colour are now written into its colour tables as well as into the theme the app paints with: 

function extendDefaultTheme(name: string, color: TLDefaultColor): void {
  const light = DEFAULT_THEME.colors.light as unknown as ColorTable
  const dark = DEFAULT_THEME.colors.dark as unknown as ColorTable
  if (!(name in light)) light[name] = color
  if (!(name in dark)) dark[name] = color
}

src/appearance/customColors.test.ts now parses a one-rectangle board through tldraw's own file parser twice — painted in teal, and in a custom colour after hydration — and this page refuses to build if the test named “reopens a board painted in a FigJam-only colour” is gone. Worth an upstream issue: parseTldrawJsonFile takes no themes, so any app with a custom palette hits this.

Task 2 · Line style is one control

FigJam's connector Line style is one 145×44 popover holding Thin Thick | Solid Dashed. The model now decides which of FigJam's two pills to copy from the same style map it always used: a connector anywhere in the selection (an arrowhead, an arrow kind, a spline, a cable routing) merges size and dash into one lineStyle control, the weight group beside the dash group with a hairline cutting the panel's full height, exactly the mechanism the Fill row already used above the palette. On a shape, FigJam's Line style is the chip row (its palette underneath is the alias §4 declines), and its size is FigJam's Font size: a 144px combobox after Typeface, with each rung listed at 12 / 13 / 14 / 16px and the chosen one checked. That reordering — Font size after Typeface, not beside Line style — was in the capture and had not been read.

Task 3 · The remaining icons

Five more icons were read off FigJam and are now in the product: the three-bar Line style trigger, the Aa Typeface trigger, the menu check mark beside a chosen list row, the picker's eyedropper, and Add text (captured for completeness, unused). Nothing else could honestly be added. The tldraw values that still fall back to a drawn glyph — draw and dotted dashes, the middle two weights, the square / pipe / bar arrowheads, eleven of twenty geo shapes, and vertical alignment — are states FigJam does not have an icon for. FigJam's library has 22 shapes and nine map; the rest (Cylinder, Document, Folder, Chevron…) have no tldraw geo value, so that is bounded by tldraw, not by the tracing. Inventing a FigJam-looking icon for a state FigJam lacks would teach a muscle memory that is wrong.

Task 4 · The mixed-selection label

Two Blocks and three shapes read “2 Blocks”, as though the Blocks had overridden the selection. It now reads “5 selected”, and the S / P / E group carries a small “2 Blocks” caption naming what it governs; a Blocks-only batch still reads “N Blocks”, so npm run test:batch is unchanged.

Task 5 · What should a Block's colour mean? (needs Zach)

A Block declares only systemsketch:* style props, so it contributes nothing to the menu and a Block-only pill has no appearance controls.

Not built, on purpose. Three readings are plausible and they are not the same feature: the header band (a tag, like FigJam's sticky colours), the border (a state, like a highlighted node), or a semantic category that the file format should own rather than a palette. Recommendation, if it has to be one: the header band, driven by tldraw's own color style added to the Block's props — it is the FigJam sticky-note idiom, it reuses this whole menu unchanged, and it survives a change of mind because the value is a stock style. The reversible default if nothing is said: leave it as it is.

Smaller calls made without asking

Opacity is FigJam's alpha mapped onto tldraw's shape opacity (§4). Huge has no tldraw rung and no row. A connector with a label keeps its no-label order; FigJam moves Line style after the text controls once a label exists. FigJam's number field under the Font size list has no value tldraw could hold and is not copied. Paste of a shape carrying a custom colour into a session that has never seen it is not handled — tldraw's paste path validates before any hook here runs — and is the one known gap. Stable (built before this pass) cannot open a board that uses a custom colour, exactly as it cannot open one in FigJam's teal; that is the same one-way door every new colour is.

Reproduce. npm run test:appearance for the browser proof and its frames; npm run check for types and the unit suites; python3 tools/figjam/emit_icons.py --check to confirm the icon module matches its captures. Rebuild this page with python3 docs/build_appearance_menu_implementation.py.

Not yet done. Rich text — bold, strikethrough, links, lists — is a separate tldraw feature with its own toolbar and is untouched here. FigJam's separate stroke weight on shapes and its shape-picker search remain the two things a stock size and a 20-entry list do not need.
